A MICHELIN-starred Italian jewel in the riverside Grund below the old town; chef Ilario Mosconi's Relais & Châteaux table (18/20 Gault&Millau) works imported Italian product into refined pasta and tasting menus overlooking the Alzette.

A pâtisserie-traiteur institution on Place Guillaume II since 1922, keeper of Luxembourgish sweet-and-savoury tradition — the autumn Quetschentaart and the Rieslingspaschtéit created here in 1928 — alongside a deep cheese and fine-food counter.

The visitor cellars of Luxembourg's biggest wine-and-crémant cooperative, on the Moselle bank at Grevenmacher and founded in 1921. Taste and buy the Grand Duchy's Riesling, Pinot and — above all — its sparkling Crémant de Luxembourg where the river marks the German border.

Trier's classic Weinstube, in the 250-year-old Palais Kesselstatt directly opposite the Liebfrauenkirche and cathedral, pouring Rieslings from the 650-year Reichsgraf von Kesselstatt estate's steep-slate Mosel/Saar/Ruwer sites alongside hearty regional cooking, self-serve at the counter. The signature Riesling-Weinstube experience of the Roman city.

A half-timbered Weinstube in Bernkastel-Kues's fairy-tale old town, named for the world-famous Bernkasteler Doctor vineyard on the slate slope above it. The place to drink Middle-Mosel Riesling — the Doctor is one of Germany's most storied sites — with Mosel trout and vintner's roast.

A cult currywurst-and-gin bar off the St. Johanner Markt using meat from Bliesgau cattle raised nearby, with vegan sauces too. Named best currywurst in Germany by the Süddeutsche Zeitung and West Germany's most popular by Falstaff (2023) — a genuine Saarbrücken institution of the young-scene kind.

places.n: Restaurant Quack in der Villa Weismüller
places.w: Creative crossover cooking in a listed Jugendstil villa with a garden terrace in Alt-Saarbrücken. A MICHELIN-Guide listing and 84 Falstaff points make it one of the city's most charming higher-end tables below the two-star bench.

Hearty Saarland home cooking and pub classics under the 120-year-old brick vaults of the neo-Gothic St. Johann town hall. A reliable, atmospheric address for Gefillde, Schwenker and regional beer in the very centre of the city.

The epitome of the Nauwieser scene — regional, seasonal cooking (around half vegetarian) with many organic and fair-trade ingredients, hidden in a linden-shaded courtyard. A daily-changing Mittagstisch by day; by evening one of the coziest wine spots in the quarter.

Authentic Neapolitan pizza on Mainzer Straße — a dough of just flour, water, little yeast and sea salt rested up to 72 hours and baked at nearly 500°C. A young local favourite for soft, airy pies both classic and creative.

Sternekoch Cliff Hämmerle serves classic French cooking with creative, vegetable-forward touches from the surrounding UNESCO Bliesgau biosphere, split between the fine 'Barrique' room and the more affordable 'Landgenuss'. One MICHELIN star, 16 points in Gault&Millau and 7 pans in GUSTO; at the Chef's Table the chef plates and explains each course himself.

A MICHELIN-starred French kitchen in a green setting in the heart of St. Ingbert, 15 minutes from Saarbrücken, led by head chef Florian Dauphin and Lorena Jil. Seasonal dishes rooted in French tradition, offered à la carte or as a menu, with six guestrooms above — one of the top addresses in the Saarpfalz.

Dillingen's upscale French address in the Stadthalle, where chef Fabrice Bertrand pairs traditional French cooking with modern, molecular flourishes (a simpler bistro 'Chez Fabrice' sits alongside). Carried by Falstaff and the state's own Saarland-erleben tourism guide — an elegant, chef-driven table in a town otherwise short on fine dining.

A brewpub right on the Saar at the Merzig marina (opened 2000) pouring three house beers — light, dark and wheat, plus a seasonal brew — with home-baked beer bread and Saarland-French brewery cooking known well beyond the town. A big beer garden with a sandy beach and playground makes it a family destination; brewery tours run on request.

A brewpub set in Neunkirchen's industrial monument beside the old blast furnace, serving the full Saarland canon — Hoorische, Gefillde, Dibbelabbes with apple sauce, Eierschmeer and the classic Lyonerpfanne — as a 'Saarländer Tapas' plate, plus house-brewed beers, Bliesgau rye bread and game from the house's own hunting grounds. A regional flag-bearer for Saarland home cooking.

An independent 'Erlebnisbrauerei' (adventure brewery) with a large brewhouse tavern, gallery and 400-seat beer garden near the Saarschleife, brewing wholesome organic beer and serving hearty, seasonal regional cooking — even with its own mustard mill. A popular stop for cyclists, hikers and families around Mettlach.
